chapter: Rene, Whitney Bank and early life
title: Whitney Bank job and where Dawson was born
summary: Dawson worked 41 years at Whitney Bank from 1917 and was born on Mandeville Street; Russell asks about Papa Laine.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: It was kind of disgusted. You mentioned about the Whitney bank. How long have you been with the Whitney bank? 41 years. Has it been the same branch all the time?

I worked at the main office about six years and after that I was transferred to the Margaret Place branch, Camp and Calio. After the bridge came in there and they had to destroy that branch then we built up a new branch on St. Charles and the Radicals, the St. Charles branch. That's the main one, right? No, that's two branches. You see the Margaret Place branch was on Camp and Calio. And the same, that was the same branch that moved over to the new place on St. Charles Street. But the main office, I started at the main office. Well at the bank right now. I started the main office I think it was 1917 before the war. I wondered if you had any other trade before that. Like this thing about old man Glennie. I was going to ask you about him. He was a painter and a lot of the men downtown were cigars.

And all. Well, all I think of it. I wanted to ask just what part of town you were born in and where you were raised. I was born on Mandible between Charles and Spain. Oh way down there. Yeah. You see Papa Lane. Do you remember Jack Lane by any chance? The white drummer who had a lot of bands and other bands.
I was born on Mandible between Charles and Spain. Oh way down there. Yeah.
